subject: Payment decline cascade, webhook lag, and dispute prevention plan
messages:
From: Oliver Sims <oliver@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: payments@acmeanalytics.com <payments@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Multiple failed charges and a disputed invoice — urgent

Hi Sean / Kimberly,

We started seeing a cascade of failed card authorizations yesterday (ALL on one batch) and Stripe has now opened two disputes for invoice #20271029. Transactions are authorizing at the acquirer level but then immediately failing with a 3DS timeout/soft-decline. I attached the invoice for reference.

A couple of notes from our team:
- Webhooks for charge.succeeded/charge.failed appear delayed in our system by ~8–10 minutes for the affected window (we have timestamps and a few retries).
- Two customers reported they attempted to update the card but the hosted update flow did not return a token.

We need:
1) Immediate guidance on dispute evidence submission for the two open disputes (we have customer correspondence and service logs).
2) A short-term way to process these paying customers (manual capture or token swap) without risking more disputes.
3) Confirmation whether Redwood can assist with a one-time card-update flow or tokenization assist.

This is time-sensitive — losing revenue and customers are pinging our finance team. Please advise next steps and who on your side will own evidence collection.

Thanks,
Oliver Sims
VP Finance, Acme Analytics
Oliver.Sims@acmeanalytics.com

Attachment: acme_invoice_20271029.pdf
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Sims <oliver@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 10:03:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Multiple failed charges and a disputed invoice — urgent

Thanks for flagging, Oliver — really sorry to hear this impact. We're treating this as a priority.

Immediate plan (24-hour window):
1) Evidence & disputes: Kimberly will own the evidence collection and upload for the two open disputes. Please send transaction IDs and any customer-facing correspondence you have (we can combine with server logs).
2) Interim collection: We can do a manual settlement path for the affected invoices. If customers can provide a new card token, we can process on your behalf; otherwise we can open a temporary invoice hold and follow a retry cadence.
3) Token update aid: we have a hosted card update UI we can spin up behind a secure link for a one-time token exchange. Kimberly, can you confirm how quickly ops can issue the link?
4) Technical follow-up: Aditya will look into the webhook delay and replay events if needed.

I will escalate to payments ops and confirm timelines. We aim to have a replay and initial dispute evidence uploaded within the next business day.

On who owns what: Kimberly (dispute evidence & hosted token link), Aditya (webhook logs + replay), Sean (escalation + coordination).

I'll follow up after Kimberly and Aditya post findings.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Sims <oliver@acmeanalytics.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 11:15:47 -0700
Subject: Re: Multiple failed charges and a disputed invoice — urgent

Hi Oliver — I pulled the Stripe dashboard and our internal webhook logs. Preliminary notes:
- There is a backlog in our webhook worker queue around 2027-11-08 22:40UTC that correlates with the failed-settle window. I've attached the raw webhook-logs snippet for the window you referenced.
- A small number of charge.failed events were retried by Stripe but did not reach our idempotency path on first delivery because the worker processed the same customer event multiple times during the backlog window.

Actionable items I can execute now:
- Collect all evidence for the two disputes (invoices, customer emails, session logs) and submit to Stripe.
- Provision a secure one-time hosted card-update link (tokenizes directly to Stripe; we can accept the token and do the capture on our side). I can generate that link within ~2 hours once you confirm which customer emails to send it to.
- Temporarily pause the retry cadence for the impacted invoice batch to avoid duplicate attempts while we replay events.

Oliver — can you confirm the customer email addresses (or a single contact) who we should send the hosted update link to? If you're OK, we'll also run a replay of the webhook events after Aditya signs off.

Attachment: webhook-logs-20271109.txt

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Payments Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Oliver Sims <oliver@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 16:20:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Multiple failed charges and a disputed invoice — urgent

Hi all — quick technical summary from infra:
- Root cause: a scheduled deploy of a worker process caused Sidekiq backlog on one of the webhook handler pools. That backlog produced an effective delivery delay of ~8–10 minutes for the events.
- Secondary issue: clock skew (~9 minutes) between the worker host and our timestamping service caused Stripe signature verification to fail on a subset of delayed events; those then retried and hit our idempotency checks inconsistently.

Remediation plan (I'll execute immediately):
1) Replay: Re-play the affected webhook batch from Stripe (we will mark the events as replayed and route them through a replay-only idempotency path).
2) Evidence: I'll collate the event payloads and package a dispute evidence packet (pdf) we can upload to Stripe — that is in progress and I will attach it when ready.
3) Mitigations: Patch the worker deployment to prevent overlapping restarts, add NTP sync checks to the worker startup, and instrument a replay-safe idempotency header in our handlers.

Estimated timeline: Replay + evidence packet upload within 12 hours; permanent mitigations deployed by end of week.

I'll follow up with the replay log and attach the dispute packet once generated.

—Aditya Rao
Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com

Attachment (pending): stripe_dispute_report_20271110.pdf
From: Oliver Sims <oliver@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Nov 2027 14:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Multiple failed charges and a disputed invoice — urgent

Thanks Sean / Kimberly / Aditya — appreciate the quick triage.

Confirming next steps from our side:
- I've attached the signed invoice and bank proof for the two disputed charges we received (acme_invoice_20271029.pdf).
- Customer contacts for the hosted update link: claire@custco.com and matt@clientcorp.com — please send the secure token links to these addresses only.
- We accept a temporary manual capture if you can tokenize the updated card and capture on our behalf; please keep us posted on PCI/consent artefacts required.

Please proceed with the replay and evidence upload. If you can confirm when replay finishes (and whether Stripe shows the events as received), we'll notify our customers to look for the hosted link and proceed with token updates.

Oliver Sims
VP Finance, Acme Analytics

Attachment: acme_invoice_20271029.pdf
